analysis.evidence: God names the object of his remembering, אֶת בְּרִיתִי, “my covenant,” and states how he will honor it. The waters will never again become a flood that destroys all flesh.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וְ introduces a Qal consecutive perfect. The ending ־תִּי marks the first person common singular. In this promise the form has future force.
Direct-object particle with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: God says he will remember the covenant between himself, his addressees, and every living creature. The promise that floodwaters will never again destroy all flesh identifies it as the covenant with Noah.
analysis.morphology: Feminine singular common noun in the construct state with a first-person singular possessive suffix.
analysis.sense: the covenant with Noah and all flesh
